collection.name: IELTS Task 2
collection.description: Essay language for IELTS Writing Task 2: stance phrases, linkers, academic verbs, hedging, and high-frequency topic vocabulary.

meta.note: Claude-authored (no external LLM). Fields map to lib/types.ts EnrichableFields; ipa intentionally left blank per captain. Packs are strictly disjoint (no word appears in more than one collection). 'category' is metadata for review/tagging.

words.definition_en: used to introduce a personal viewpoint
words.example_simple: In my opinion, public transport should be free.
words.example_complex: In my opinion, the benefits of remote working clearly outweigh its drawbacks for most employees.

words.definition_en: used to signal that what follows is one's own standpoint
words.example_simple: From my perspective, both sides have valid points.
words.example_complex: From my perspective, governments should prioritise prevention over punishment when tackling youth crime.

words.definition_en: a strong way to state a personal conviction
words.example_simple: I firmly believe that education should be free.
words.example_complex: I firmly believe that investing in renewable energy is the most effective response to climate change.

words.vi_meaning: đối với tôi có vẻ như
words.definition_en: a softer way to introduce an opinion
words.example_simple: It seems to me that both options have risks.
words.example_complex: It seems to me that stricter regulation, rather than an outright ban, would strike a better balance.

words.vi_meaning: không còn nghi ngờ gì rằng
words.definition_en: used to present something as certain or undeniable
collocations: there is no doubt that technology
words.example_simple: There is no doubt that exercise improves health.
words.example_complex: There is no doubt that globalisation has reshaped local economies, though its effects are unevenly distributed.

words.definition_en: to publicly support an idea or policy; a person who does so
words.example_simple: Many people advocate free healthcare.
words.example_complex: Those who advocate stricter gun laws argue that they reduce violent crime.

words.definition_en: to support a particular idea or proposal
collocations: be in favour of the policy
words.example_simple: I am in favour of longer school holidays.
words.example_complex: While some are in favour of nuclear power, others regard the risks as unacceptable.

words.definition_en: to disagree with or resist an idea
words.example_simple: Many residents are opposed to the new road.
words.example_complex: Critics who are opposed to zoos contend that no enclosure can replicate an animal's natural habitat.

words.vi_meaning: thừa nhận (điều bất lợi cho lập luận)
words.definition_en: to admit that an opposing point is partly true
words.example_simple: I concede that cars are convenient.
words.example_complex: Although one must concede that social media has downsides, its capacity to connect people is undeniable.

words.definition_en: used to add a further supporting point
words.example_simple: Furthermore, it saves money.
words.example_complex: Furthermore, remote learning gives students in rural areas access to resources they would otherwise lack.

words.definition_en: used to introduce an additional and often stronger point
words.example_simple: Moreover, it is good for the environment.
words.example_complex: Moreover, a shorter working week could improve productivity as well as employees' wellbeing.

words.definition_en: used to add another point
words.example_simple: In addition, it creates jobs.
words.example_complex: In addition to reducing traffic, cycling infrastructure encourages a healthier lifestyle.

words.definition_en: used to introduce a contrasting idea
words.example_simple: However, there are some problems.
words.example_complex: This approach is efficient; however, it overlooks the needs of low-income families.

words.definition_en: in spite of what has just been said
words.example_simple: It is expensive. Nevertheless, it is worth it.
words.example_complex: The policy is controversial; nevertheless, its long-term benefits justify the initial cost.

words.definition_en: used to introduce the opposing side of an argument
collocations: on the one hand ... on the other hand
words.example_simple: On the other hand, some people disagree.
words.example_complex: On the other hand, opponents claim that such subsidies distort the market and burden taxpayers.

words.definition_en: used to show a clear difference between two things
words.example_simple: In contrast, cities are crowded.
words.example_complex: In contrast to previous generations, today's students face intense pressure to specialise early.
words.false_friend_note: Not the same as 'on the contrary', which corrects a false statement rather than comparing two things.

words.definition_en: used to compare or contrast two facts
words.example_simple: Some like the city, whereas others prefer the countryside.
words.example_complex: Wealthy nations can fund green technology, whereas poorer ones often struggle to meet basic needs.

words.definition_en: used to introduce a result or effect
words.example_simple: It rained, and consequently the match was cancelled.
words.example_complex: Fossil fuels are being depleted; consequently, the shift to renewable sources has become urgent.

words.definition_en: for that reason; as a logical result
words.example_simple: The plan failed; therefore we need a new one.
words.example_complex: Traffic congestion harms both health and the economy; governments should therefore invest in public transport.

words.definition_en: because of this; as a consequence
words.example_simple: Sales fell, and as a result the shop closed.
words.example_complex: Automation is replacing routine jobs, and as a result many workers must retrain to stay employable.

words.definition_en: used to introduce an example
words.example_simple: Many sports, for instance football, build teamwork.
words.example_complex: Some cities, for instance Amsterdam, have shown that prioritising cyclists can transform urban life.

words.definition_en: without being affected by something
words.example_simple: Despite the rain, they kept playing.
words.example_complex: Despite significant investment, the initiative failed to reduce poverty in the region.
words.false_friend_note: Followed by a noun or -ing, not a full clause: 'despite being tired', not 'despite he was tired'.

words.definition_en: used to express purpose
words.example_simple: We save money in order to travel.
words.example_complex: In order to curb obesity, some governments have introduced a tax on sugary drinks.

words.definition_en: used to introduce the final summary of an essay
words.example_simple: In conclusion, I support the idea.
words.example_complex: In conclusion, while both approaches have merit, education is a more sustainable solution than punishment.

words.definition_en: used to summarise the main points
words.example_simple: To sum up, the plan has clear benefits.
words.example_complex: To sum up, the evidence suggests that prevention is both cheaper and more humane than punishment.

words.vi_meaning: giải quyết, đối phó với (vấn đề)
words.definition_en: to deal with or tackle a problem
words.example_simple: The city must address pollution.
words.example_complex: To address rising inequality, governments need policies that go beyond short-term relief.

words.vi_meaning: vượt trội hơn, quan trọng hơn
words.definition_en: to be greater in value or importance than something else
words.example_simple: The benefits outweigh the costs.
words.example_complex: For most families, the advantages of relocating clearly outweigh the disruption it causes.

words.vi_meaning: có thể cho rằng, được cho là
words.definition_en: used to say something can reasonably be argued
words.example_simple: It is arguably the best solution.
words.example_complex: Education is arguably the single most effective tool for lifting communities out of poverty.

words.vi_meaning: ở một mức độ nào đó
words.definition_en: partly but not completely
words.example_simple: This is true to some extent.
words.example_complex: While automation threatens jobs to some extent, it also creates new roles that did not exist before.

words.definition_en: to be likely to behave in a particular way, generally
words.example_simple: Prices tend to rise in summer.
words.example_complex: Students who receive early feedback tend to perform better in their final assessments.

words.definition_en: a cautious way to introduce a debatable claim
words.example_simple: It can be argued that both are important.
words.example_complex: It can be argued that access to the internet has become as essential as access to clean water.

words.definition_en: generally speaking; on the whole
words.example_simple: By and large, the plan worked well.
words.example_complex: By and large, the policy has succeeded, though a minority of residents remain dissatisfied.

words.definition_en: to a moderate degree, in comparison with something else
words.example_simple: The cost is relatively low.
words.example_complex: Although relatively expensive at first, solar panels become cost-effective within a decade.

words.definition_en: large or important enough to have an effect
words.example_simple: There was a significant change.
words.example_complex: Immigration has had a significant impact on the country's cultural and economic landscape.

words.definition_en: existing or happening over a large area or among many people
words.example_simple: Smartphone use is widespread.
words.example_complex: There is widespread agreement that current levels of consumption are environmentally unsustainable.

words.definition_en: causing harm or damage
words.example_simple: Too much sugar is detrimental to health.
words.example_complex: Excessive screen time can be detrimental to children's sleep and concentration.

words.definition_en: long-term shifts in temperature and weather patterns, largely human-caused
words.example_simple: Climate change affects everyone.
words.example_complex: Tackling climate change requires coordinated action from governments, businesses and individuals alike.

words.vi_meaning: lượng khí thải carbon (dấu chân carbon)
words.definition_en: the amount of carbon dioxide a person or activity produces
words.example_simple: Flying increases your carbon footprint.
words.example_complex: Consumers can lower their carbon footprint by eating less meat and choosing local produce.

words.definition_en: energy from sources that are not depleted, such as sun and wind
words.example_simple: Renewable energy is becoming cheaper.
words.example_complex: Shifting to renewable energy would reduce both pollution and dependence on imported fuel.

words.definition_en: able to continue without harming the environment or resources
words.example_simple: We need sustainable farming.
words.example_complex: Sustainable development seeks to meet present needs without compromising future generations.

words.definition_en: stress caused by demands to perform well in study
words.example_simple: Students face academic pressure.
words.example_complex: Intense academic pressure can undermine the very creativity that education is meant to nurture.

words.definition_en: the subjects and content taught in a school or course
words.example_simple: The curriculum includes science and art.
words.example_complex: Many argue that the national curriculum should include practical skills such as budgeting and cooking.

words.definition_en: education that teaches practical skills for a specific job
words.example_simple: Vocational training leads to real jobs.
words.example_complex: Expanding vocational training could reduce youth unemployment more quickly than pushing everyone towards university.

words.vi_meaning: năng lực số, hiểu biết về công nghệ
words.definition_en: the ability to use digital technology effectively and safely
words.example_simple: Digital literacy is now essential.
words.example_complex: Without adequate digital literacy, older citizens risk being excluded from essential online services.

words.definition_en: close watching of people, often by authorities or cameras
words.example_simple: The city uses surveillance cameras.
words.example_complex: Widespread surveillance may deter crime, but it also raises serious concerns about personal privacy.

words.definition_en: the use of machines and technology to do work instead of people
words.example_simple: Automation is changing factories.
words.example_complex: As automation spreads, workers will increasingly need to develop skills that machines cannot easily replicate.

words.definition_en: something that discourages people from doing something wrong
words.example_simple: Fines act as a deterrent.
words.example_complex: Supporters of harsh sentencing claim it serves as a deterrent, though the evidence is far from conclusive.

words.vi_meaning: sự cải tạo, phục hồi (tội phạm)
words.definition_en: the process of helping offenders return to normal life
words.example_simple: Prisons should focus on rehabilitation.
words.example_complex: A justice system built around rehabilitation rather than punishment tends to lower reoffending rates.

words.definition_en: the number of crimes committed in a place over a period
words.example_simple: The crime rate fell last year.
words.example_complex: Cities that invest in youth programmes often see a marked drop in the crime rate over time.

words.definition_en: the condition of being severely overweight
words.example_simple: Obesity is a growing problem.
words.example_complex: Rising obesity places an enormous strain on healthcare systems already stretched to their limits.

words.definition_en: a way of living with little physical activity
words.example_simple: A sedentary lifestyle harms health.
words.example_complex: The shift towards a sedentary lifestyle, driven by desk jobs and screens, has fuelled a range of chronic illnesses.

words.definition_en: medical services provided or funded by the government
words.example_simple: Public healthcare should be free.
words.example_complex: Well-funded public healthcare ensures that treatment depends on need rather than the ability to pay.

words.definition_en: the level of comfort and wealth a person or group has
words.example_simple: Their standard of living improved.
words.example_complex: Economic growth has raised the standard of living for many, yet the gains remain unevenly shared.

words.definition_en: the unequal distribution of income across a society
words.example_simple: Income inequality is rising.
words.example_complex: Growing income inequality can erode social cohesion and fuel political instability.

words.definition_en: the process by which economies and cultures become interconnected worldwide
words.example_simple: Globalisation connects markets.
words.example_complex: Globalisation has lifted millions out of poverty while also threatening local traditions and industries.

words.definition_en: the growth of towns and cities as people move from the countryside
words.example_simple: Urbanisation is speeding up.
words.example_complex: Rapid urbanisation has outpaced infrastructure, leaving many cities struggling with congestion and housing shortages.

words.definition_en: the basic systems and services a society needs, such as roads and power
words.example_simple: The city needs better infrastructure.
words.example_complex: Reliable infrastructure is a precondition for economic growth, yet many developing nations lack the funds to build it.

words.vi_meaning: cân bằng công việc và cuộc sống
words.definition_en: a healthy division between time spent working and on personal life
words.example_simple: A good work-life balance reduces stress.
words.example_complex: Flexible hours and remote options can help employees achieve a healthier work-life balance.

words.definition_en: a fixed limit or share that is officially allowed or required
words.example_simple: The country set an import quota.
words.example_complex: Some argue that hiring quotas promote fairness, while others believe they undermine merit.

words.definition_en: money paid by a government to support an industry or lower a price
words.example_simple: Farmers receive a subsidy.
words.example_complex: Fuel subsidies keep prices low for consumers but can discourage the switch to cleaner energy.

words.definition_en: the presence of harmful substances in the environment
words.example_simple: Air pollution is a serious problem in big cities.
words.example_complex: Traffic is a major source of pollution, which in turn harms public health and the climate.

words.definition_en: the clearing of forests on a large scale
words.example_simple: Deforestation destroys animal habitats.
words.example_complex: Widespread deforestation not only threatens biodiversity but also accelerates climate change.

words.definition_en: the state of not having a job
words.example_simple: Unemployment rose during the crisis.
words.example_complex: Rising youth unemployment can lead to social unrest if it is left unaddressed.

words.definition_en: a system in which the government provides social and financial support
words.example_simple: The welfare state supports those in need.
words.example_complex: Supporters argue that a strong welfare state reduces poverty, while critics claim it discourages work.

words.definition_en: a person's emotional and psychological well-being
words.example_simple: Exercise is good for mental health.
words.example_complex: Growing awareness of mental health has encouraged more people to seek professional help.

words.definition_en: the ability to analyse information and form reasoned judgements
words.example_simple: Schools should teach critical thinking.
words.example_complex: Rather than memorising facts, students benefit far more from developing critical thinking skills.

words.definition_en: computer systems able to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence
words.example_simple: Artificial intelligence is changing many jobs.
words.example_complex: While artificial intelligence boosts efficiency, it also raises concerns about job losses and privacy.

words.definition_en: to make people more informed about an issue
words.example_simple: The campaign raised awareness of recycling.
words.example_complex: Governments can raise public awareness of environmental issues through education and the media.
